results.title: USA Basketball back atop FIBA men's world rankings, overtaking Spain for No. 1
excerpts:
forward Mikal Bridges (5) gestures during the Basketball World Cup quarterfinal game between Italy and U.S. at the Mall of Asia Arena in Manila, Philippines, Tuesday, Sept. 5, 2023. (AP Photo/Michael Conroy)

USA Basketball is back atop the FIBA men’s world rankings, even after failing to medal at the World Cup.

The Americans flipped spots with Spain for No. 1 in the world in the updated rankings that were released Friday, reclaiming the top spot that they lost late last year. Spain is now No. 2, and World Cup champion Germany soared eight spots to No. 3 on the world list — the best in that program's history.

Recommended Videos

* * *

It's certainly possible now that the Americans will keep the top spot leading into the Paris Olympics, where the U.S. will aim for a fifth consecutive gold medal. FIBA, the sport's governing body, updates its rankings every few months; Friday's update was the first tweak to the men's list since February.

Spain had overtaken the U.S.
in November 2022, ending a 12-year run in the top spot for the Americans.

“The world is good at basketball,” U.S. point guard Jalen Brunson of the New York Knicks said as the World Cup was winding down. “Respect everybody.”

FIBA’s rankings were changed in 2017 to a system that only takes results from the most recent eight years into account. The Olympic golds from Rio de Janeiro and Tokyo factor into the current rankings, and obviously help after back-to-back failures to medal at the last two World Cups — the U.S. was seventh at China in 2019 and fourth in Manila earlier this month, falling to Germany in the semifinals and Canada in the bronze-medal game.

Canada soared nine spots to No. 6 in the world after winning that bronze, and Latvia — which made the quarterfinals of its first World Cup — climbed 22 spots to No. 8.

The top 10 teams are the U.S., Spain, Germany, Australia (which slipped one spot to No.
4), World Cup silver medalist Serbia (which climbed one spot to No. 5), Canada, Argentina (down three spots to No. 7 after not even making the World Cup field), Latvia, France (down four spots to No. 9) and Lithuania (down four spots to No. 10).

The biggest climber in the rankings after the World Cup was South Sudan, which was No. 63 in the world before the tournament and moved up 32 spots to No. 31. South Sudan qualified for the Paris Olympics after ending the World Cup as the best finisher from Africa at the tournament.

“This team is a beam of light, like I keep on saying,” South Sudan coach Royal Ivey said after his team clinched the Olympic berth in Manila. “We’re bringing unity, camaraderie, love and friendship to this country.”

Latvia was the second-biggest climber, rising 22 spots, and Cape Verde — which got a win at the World Cup — improved its ranking 19 spots to No. 46.
“We made a statement," Cape Verde’s Will Tavares, a Rhode Island-born forward, said after the World Cup win. "Even though we’re the smallest country, we have so much heart.”

There are 159 men's teams in the FIBA rankings. USA Basketball also is ranked No. 1 in the other three sets of rankings maintained by FIBA — women, boys and girls, all by wide margins.

# Germany jump to No. 2 in latest FIBA World Ranking Men, presented by Nike

5 min to read Press Release

The FIBA World Ranking, presented by Nike has been updated after the conclusion of the Continental Cups.

MIES (Switzerland) - USA remained the number one country in the [FIBA World Ranking Men](https://www.fiba.basketball/en/ranking/men) , which has a new No. 2 as Germany rose one spot after claiming the [FIBA EuroBasket 2025](https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025) title in spectacular fashion, finishing the tournament as invincible European champions.

[Paris 2024](https://www.fiba.

...

AmeriCup 2025 runners-up Argentina and Lithuania follow, ahead of Brazil, who used their title-winning AmeriCup run to move up two levels into the top 10.

Türkiye were the biggest risers in the top 50, rising from 27th to 12th after reaching their first EuroBasket Final since 2001. They got past Latvia, Czechia, former number two Serbia, Poland, and Greece - all higher-ranked opponents.

Greece claimed a historic medal but also lost to Bosnia and Herzegovina and Türkiye, beating only one higher-ranked team - Spain - during the tournament.

Finland moved up from 20th to 17th thanks to their first-ever continental Semi-Finals appearance, achieving the second-highest score increase in the Top 20 behind Türkiye.

FIBA Asia Cup 2025 bronze medalists Iran advanced by two places, reaching 26th, while finalists China shifted up three positions to 27th.

[FIBA AfroBasket 2025](https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-afrobasket-2025) champions Angola progressed from 33rd to 29th.
They went undefeated on home soil, but aside from South Sudan, they only beat teams ranked lower than themselves. Senegal rose from 47th to 45th after securing the bronze at the continental tournament.

The biggest standout among all countries was Mali, who rode their silver medal at AfroBasket 2025 to leap 18 spots, reaching 65th in the world.

Other notable improvers included Sweden and Portugal, who each surged by nine positions - to 40th and 47th, respectively - after reaching the Round of 16 at EuroBasket 2025. In the Americas, Uruguay were the highest climber among the top-ranked teams, jumping seven levels to 44th following their 7th-place at the AmeriCup 2025.

Last but not least, Jamaica earned a spot in the [FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027 Americas Qualifiers](https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-basketball-world-cup-2027-americas-qualifiers) through the Pre-Qualifiers, going from 107th to 95th place in the process.
For more information about the method used in the calculation of the FIBA World Ranking Men, please refer to the ' [How it Works](https://assets.fiba.basketball/image/upload/documents-events-world-fiba-ranking-men-how-it-works.pdf) ' section.

# FIBA Men's World Ranking

Ara Eve Leo Sal

1x

The FIBA Men's World Ranking is an official ranking system maintained by the International Basketball Federation ( FIBA ) that evaluates the performance of senior men's national basketball teams worldwide based on their results in international competitions over an eight-year period.
[[[1]]()]() Introduced in September 2010 following the FIBA Basketball World Cup in Turkey , the ranking provides a dynamic assessment of team strength to guide seeding, qualifications, and host allocations for major events like the Olympics, World Cup , and continental championships. [[[2]]()]() The ranking employs a game-based methodology launched in October 2017, which calculates points for each match using a formula that incorporates base points for wins or losses (ranging from 250 to 750 depending on margin of victory or defeat), adjustments for home/away status (±50 points), and opposition strength relative to pre-game rankings. [[[3]]()]() [[[4]]()]() These rating points are then weighted by factors including time decay (full weight for the current and previous year, decreasing to zero after eight years), competition importance (e.g., 2.5 for the World Cup, 2 for the Olympics), tournament stage (1 for main rounds, 0.

...

[[[8]]()]() These limitations prompted the transition to a more detailed, game \-based evaluation in 2017.

### 2017 Reforms and Evolution

In February 2017, FIBA President Horacio Muratore announced a transformative new competition system set to launch in November 2017, which included a comprehensive overhaul of the men's world ranking methodology as part of broader calendar reforms. [[[9]]()]() This initiative coincided with a strategic 11-year partnership with Nike, announced on February 28, 2017, designating Nike as the title sponsor for the rankings to enhance their visibility and global reach. [[[10]]()]() The primary motivations for the 2017 reforms stemmed from longstanding criticisms of the prior system, which failed to include all national teams, employed an outdated weighting scheme focused on tournament final standings, treated all results equally over an eight-year period regardless of recency, and overlooked performances in qualifier matches.

...

[[[4]]()]() This structure ensures that inter-regional games in lower-weighted zones do not disproportionately affect rankings compared to high-profile international events. Stage weight ($ S $) differentiates the importance of preliminary phases from main tournament play. Games in the primary tournament phase are weighted at 1.0, qualifiers at 0.5, pre-qualifiers at 0.25, and special categories like European small countries tournaments at 0.15. [[[4]]()]() These values underscore the greater significance of results in core competition stages over preparatory or lower-tier matches. Round weight ($ R $) applies exclusively to top competitions such as the World Cup , Olympics, and continental cups, increasing with advancement to reward deeper tournament runs. It starts at 1.0 for the first round, rises to 2.0 for the second round, 4.0 for the third round (e.g., quarterfinals), and reaches 6.0 for the fourth and fifth rounds (e.g., semifinals and final).

...

The FIBA Men's World Ranking operates on an 8-year rolling window, incorporating rating points from all official FIBA-sanctioned senior men's international games during that period, excluding club competitions, friendly matches, and basketball events in multi-sport competitions other than the Olympic Basketball Tournament. [[[4]]()]() [[[8]]()]() This cycle ensures that recent performances carry greater weight through time decay factors applied to older games, while games exceeding eight years are discarded to reflect current team strengths. [[[4]]()]() Updates to the ranking occur after every international window or the conclusion of major tournaments, such as qualifiers and continental cups, enabling near-real-time adjustments based on new results; this frequency was introduced in December 2017 with the adoption of the game-based system.

...

The shared calculation framework with the men's rankings allows for parallel methodologies while focusing exclusively on women's events. [[[16]]()]() The ranking is updated with the same frequency as the men's, typically after international windows and the conclusion of major competitions, enabling real-time reflections of team progress. As of the latest update in August 2025, the United States holds the top spot with 880.9 points, followed by Australia at 719.6 points, underscoring the dominance of these programs in recent cycles. Historically, women's teams have played fewer official games compared to their male counterparts, which can introduce greater volatility in rankings and heightens the impact of results from key events like Olympic qualifying tournaments. This aspect emphasizes the role of consistent participation in building stable positions.

...

Updates occur simultaneously after key events like qualifiers and major tournaments, promoting fairness in global assessments. This shared approach replaced earlier competition-based models, enabling more precise reflections of game outcomes across 164 men's and 131 women's teams. [[[4]]()]() [[[16]]()]() [[[8]]()]() [[[17]]()]() Despite these similarities, divergences exist to accommodate structural differences in men's and women's international basketball . The women's ranking , first published in 2016, predates the men's current iteration but adopted its formula later; the men's original system began in 2010. Basis points scales differ slightly, with women's values lower overall (e.g., 600 for a 1-9 point win versus 650 for men, 200 for a 20+ point loss versus 250) to reflect fewer high-stakes opportunities and potentially closer contests. Regional competition weights are calibrated for women's continental imbalances, assigning 0.9 to Asia / Oceania (versus men's 0.

...

By 2025, both rankings are seamlessly integrated on the FIBA website, facilitating cross-comparisons and underscoring the organization's commitment to parity. [[[8]]()]() [[[17]]()]() [[[11]]()]() [[[1]]()]() [[[18]]()]()

## Current Standings

### Top 10 Teams as of 2025

As of November 2025, following the conclusion of major continental tournaments such as the FIBA EuroBasket , AmeriCup, and Asia Cup , the FIBA Men's World Ranking provides a current snapshot of the top-performing national teams based on accumulated points from international competitions. The United States continues to lead the rankings, a position reinforced by their gold medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics and strong showings in subsequent events. [[[6]]()]() The top 10 teams are as follows:

Germany's rise to second place stems from their undefeated run to win the 2025 FIBA EuroBasket , marking a significant boost after their 2023 World Cup triumph. Serbia maintains third through consistent European performances, even after an early elimination at EuroBasket 2025\. These rankings reflect weighted results from games over an eight-year period, emphasizing recent achievements in FIBA-sanctioned events. [[[6]]()]() [[[4]]()]()

### Recent Changes and Trends

The 2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup marked a pivotal shift in the rankings, with Germany surging 10 positions to third place after clinching the tournament title on home soil, while the United States reclaimed the top spot despite securing bronze, moving up from second. This event highlighted the impact of major tournaments on mid-tier teams, as Germany's victory propelled them ahead of traditional powers like Argentina , which dropped from fourth to fifth.
